label: token p as the first input (t=0)
explanation: Fires at saturating, near-constant magnitude (~1.89) whenever the first original token (t=0) is p; this accounts for 99.4% of activation mass, with precision 1.0. A weak residual (~0.05x max) fires when p is the second token (t=1) and the first token is one of k, w, c, t. It does not fire on p at t=1 after any other first token, on p at t>=2, during the delimiter or copy phase (including when p is being output), or on any other token. The simpler predicate (t==0)&(in_tok==p) gets F1 0.94 and mass recall 0.994.

issues: Small overclaim: the explanation says the feature never fires in the copy phase 'even when p is the token being output'. Dev has 9 copy-phase activations and test has 26 missed steps. Most are weak re-fires (0.03-0.19x max) on step L+1, where the original first token p is fed back as input, mostly in sequences whose second token is c. These carry 0.0% of the activation mass, so this is a small repeated pattern rather than a gap that matters.

Verified: p at t=0 has precision 1.0 (16580 of 16580 dev steps). p at t=1 after k/w/c/t has precision 1.0 (2209 steps, 0.6% of the mass). p at t=1 after any other first token has precision 0.0 (14514 steps). The feature never fires on non-p tokens or at the delimiter step. Test scores reproduce: precision 1.0, recall 0.9986, mass recall 0.9999, no false positives.
